# Proverbs 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** When you sit down to eat with someone powerful, pay close attention to what's really going on.

**2** If you tend to overindulge, you'd better put a knife to your own throat.

**3** Don't be seduced by their fancy food — it's bait.

**4** Don't exhaust yourself trying to get rich. Have the sense to stop.

**5** The moment you focus on wealth, it disappears — it literally grows wings and flies away like an eagle.

**6** Don't eat with a stingy person, and don't be tempted by their fancy food,

**7** Because they're calculating every bite you take. They say, 'Help yourself!' but they resent every morsel.

**8** You'll end up sick to your stomach, and all your kind words will have been wasted.

**9** Don't bother trying to explain something to a fool — they'll just look down on everything you say.

**10** Don't move an ancient boundary stone, and don't encroach on land belonging to orphans,

**11** Because their Defender is powerful — He will take up their case against you personally.

**12** Commit yourself to learning, and open your ears to words of knowledge.

**13** Don't hold back discipline from a child — a spanking won't kill them.

**14** Disciplining them now could save their life later.

**15** My child, if you grow wise, you'll make my heart overflow with joy —

**16** My whole being will celebrate when you speak what's right and true.

**17** Don't waste your energy envying people who do wrong. Instead, keep your reverence for the LORD burning all day long,

**18** Because there is definitely a future ahead, and your hope will not be disappointed.

**19** Listen, my child — be wise, and set your heart firmly on the right road.

**20** Don't hang around with heavy drinkers or people who gorge themselves on food,

**21** Because drunks and gluttons end up broke, and their laziness dresses them in rags.

**22** Listen to your father — he gave you life. Don't look down on your mother when she's old.

**23** Invest in truth and never sell it. Buy wisdom, discipline, and understanding at any price.

**24** A righteous child brings tremendous joy to their father. A parent of a wise child is truly happy.

**25** Make your father and mother proud! Give the woman who brought you into the world something to celebrate.

**26** My child, give me your full attention. Watch how I live and follow my example.

**27** A prostitute is a deep pit, and an unfaithful woman is a trap with no way out.

**28** She hides and waits like a mugger, adding to the number of unfaithful people in the world.

**29** Who's miserable? Who's full of regret? Who's always fighting? Who's always complaining? Who has injuries they can't explain? Who has bloodshot eyes?

**30** The people who spend their evenings with wine, sampling one exotic drink after another.

**31** Don't be mesmerized by wine — how it glows red in the cup, how smoothly it goes down.

**32** Because in the end it bites you like a snake and poisons you like a viper.

**33** Your eyes will see things that aren't there, and your mind will say things that make no sense.

**34** You'll feel like you're lying on a bed in the middle of the ocean, swaying on top of a ship's mast.

**35** You'll say, 'They hit me, but I didn't feel it! They beat me, but I don't remember! When can I wake up so I can have another drink?'

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **23:5**: Incredible image — money literally sprouts wings and flies away. You can't hold onto it by grasping harder; it has a life of its own.

- **23:7**: This is about reading people — the stingy host says 'eat up!' but they're counting every bite in their head. Listen to the heart, not the words.

- **23:29-35**: The greatest anti-drinking passage ever written. It starts with six haunting questions and ends with the addict's tragic punchline: 'When can I have another drink?'

— PNEUMA
